title: StaticBody2D not completely static
body:
<!-- Failed to upload "2025-07-22 23-50-20.mp4" -->

### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.4.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS 24.04 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 760M (radeonsi, gfx1103_r1, LLVM 19.1.1, DRM 3.57, 6.8.0-64-generic) - AMD Ryzen 5 7640U w/ Radeon 760M Graphics (12 threads)

### Issue description

Every now and then, a `StaticBody2D` is moved slightly by collision(s) in a direction that is not even coded.

In my case, I remade Pong with StaticBody2Ds. I've seen the paddle's x coordinate a bit off when the ball was stuck between the paddle and the boundary. It only happens rarely but I've seen it more than once.

### Steps to reproduce

~~I will try to find out how/if this can be reproduced consistenly.
This (steps + MRP) will be updated then.~~

~~In the meantime, maybe someone else has also encountered this issue?
Any help figuring out an MRP is appreciated as well, I can provide the current code.~~

Tried to reduce it as much as possible, maybe even too much...
(I have recorded a short video of the original to show the issue but am unable to upload it here, probably because I don't know why... Drag and drop does not work. If it still needed, I'll upload it elsewhere and just add the link.)
The paddle can be moved with UI up/down.
All you need to do is push the ball upwards (y-) a few times.
Once it's x position changes, the debugger will show an error every time it is pushed.

In the "real" game, the paddle would try pushing the ball away if it's above or below.
This is not implemented here since it's not part of the issue.
Yet here, it causes the ball to be "stronger" than the paddle so that it just pushes it away, even if it's speed is lower. Is this expected?
